newsitem.title: UK: New poll gives UK's Labour hefty 24-point lead.
newsitem.headline: New poll gives UK's Labour hefty 24-point lead.

text.p: Britain's opposition Labour party has a hefty 24 point opinion poll lead over the ruling Conservatives just five days before a May 1 election, according to a survey carried out for the Sunday Mirror newspaper.

A spokesman for the paper said the MORI poll put Labour on 53 percent, down two percentage points from a similar survey it carried out three weeks ago, while backing for the Conservatives dropped one point to 29 percent.
Support for the minority Liberal Democrats was up three points to 12 percent.
If Labour can maintain the double-digit lead it has enjoyed in every poll bar one during the five week campaign, party leader Tony Blair will be prime minister with a huge parliamentary majority.
When asked by MORI who should be the country's next leader, 38 percent said Blair -- down one point from three weeks ago -- while 26 percent said Major, also down one point.
MORI interviewed 1,070 people on Wednesday and Thursday.
